- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to align with momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish; add 0.5–1.5% bias to early periods.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, model lags in correction; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and reduce slope of decline.
- Mean reversion is often overestimated; if price is above 3σ from recent mean, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until reversion.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate volatility; cap forecast at 1.5–2σ above recent 14-day moving average to avoid extreme outliers.
